Hi Emma — thanks for the clear asks. Below are two sections: a one-paragraph customer-facing summary you can paste into the SOW, followed by an engineering note with exact defaults and deletion paths.

Customer-friendly paragraph (SOW):
Redwood does not share customer prompts or outputs with third parties and stores request and response logs only to operate and troubleshoot the service. For our hosted Redwood API, logs are retained by default for 30 days to support debugging, quality monitoring, and regression alerts; customers on Dedicated or Private deployments can configure or disable retention to meet their policies. All logs for hosted deployments are kept in the cloud region you select; we can provide a Data Processing Addendum with residency commitments for enterprise contracts.

Engineering note (detailed defaults):
- Hosted (Redwood API): by default, request/response artifacts (prompts, model responses, metadata such as request timestamps and model_version) are retained for 30 days. Retention is counted from ingestion time and enforced automatically via TTL.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): logs are retained according to the customer's contract; default config for Dedicated trial accounts is 90 days, but customers can set a TTL or enable immediate purge.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Redwood control plane can be configured to not persist verbose logs; many customers run with no cross-customer logging by default.
- Prompts vs outputs: we treat both as request/response artifacts; there is no separate "permanent prompts" bucket unless the customer explicitly opts-in (e.g., for evals or fine-tuning).
- Deletion options: customers can invoke the Delete API for a given conversation_id (immediate), submit a retention purge job via Console (scheduled), or ask Redwoods ops to run a one-time purge for compliance. Enrollment in auto-deletion (short TTL) is configurable per-tenant.
- Residency: logs for hosted accounts are stored in the region selected at account creation and not replicated to other regions by default. Replication may be enabled for high-availability plans and is subject to contract terms.

Attachments: I attached a short PDF summary for procurement. Let me know if you want a slightly more conservative default (e.g., 14 days) for the draft SOW.
